Reframed take with SLOOS context:
- Policy stance remains a hawkish hold: the Committee kept the funds rate at 5–5.25% and continued QT while signaling possible “additional policy firming.”
- SLOOS signals a more material credit drag than the statement alone: banks tightened standards and terms across consumer (auto, RRE/HELOC, subprime, other), C&I, and CRE; widened spreads on nonfarm nonresidential and multifamily; lowered LTVs and raised DSCRs; and pushed up loan rates. Reported reasons include a weaker economic outlook, higher funding costs, deposit outflows, and liquidity concerns. Demand weakened for C&I uses (plant/equipment, M&A, inventory, A/R financing). Banks broadly expect to tighten further.
- Cross-cuts: mid-sized banks cited economic outlook and liquidity positions; foreign banks tightened spreads and expect further C&I tightening; largest banks tightened credit card lending on credit quality concerns.
- Implication: While jobs and unemployment remain favorable, SLOOS indicates tighter credit conditions and rising risk aversion that should weigh on activity and hiring, reinforcing the statement’s caution and amplifying transmission lags. Net tone is more cautious than the headline “sound and resilient” language suggests.
